response.text:
Short answer: the CSV will not keep formulas or inter-sheet links — it will only contain the last calculated values — so you need to make sure those values are correct and exported in the format the finance portal expects. Below is a focused checklist and recommended steps.

Immediate risks to watch for
- Formulas lost: CSV stores cell values only. All SUMIFs and other formulas will disappear. If you need formulas kept, CSV is the wrong format.
- External references: formulas that reference another sheet/workbook will export only their last-calculated values. If those source cells change later, the CSV won't update.
- Stale calculations: if formulas haven’t been recalculated, exported values may be out-of-date.
- Date/number locale and formatting: dates, decimals, thousands separators, currency symbols, and percent formats can change meaning when saved as CSV.
- Delimiters and special characters: commas, quotes, and line breaks inside text cells can break CSV structure unless handled correctly.
- Leading zeros and large numbers: IDs and long numeric strings can lose leading zeros or convert to scientific notation.
- Hidden/filtered rows or columns: hidden data might not be obvious and might be omitted or included depending on how you export.
- Encoding: wrong character encoding (non-UTF-8) can corrupt special characters.
- Single-sheet limitation: CSV can only contain one sheet — any references to other sheets won’t be preserved.

Recommended step-by-step workflow (safe order)
1. Make a backup copy of the workbook and/or the tab (save a copy named like Budget_for_export.xlsx).
2. Verify portal requirements: required columns, headers, delimiter (comma/semicolon), encoding (UTF-8), date format, decimal separator, rounding rules, and whether they want text or numeric fields.
3. Force a full recalculation so values are current:
   - Excel: Ctrl+Alt+F9 (recalculate all).
   - Google Sheets recalculates automatically but double-check volatile functions.
4. Resolve external references:
   - If SUMIFs reference another sheet in the same workbook, ensure that sheet is correct and up-to-date.
   - If references point to another workbook, either open that workbook and recalc, or copy the source ranges into the same workbook so values are correct, or replace formulas with values (next step).
   - Consider breaking links (Data → Edit Links → Break Links in Excel) only after you’re sure values are correct.
5. Work on a copy and convert formulas to values:
   - Select the whole export sheet → Copy → Paste Special → Values. This ensures the CSV will contain the intended numbers.
   - Keep the original file with formulas for audit/updates.
6. Fix formatting for export:
   - Dates: convert to a stable format (ISO yyyy-mm-dd) to avoid locale problems.
   - Numbers: remove thousands separators (or ensure portal accepts them). Set decimals/rounding to portal
